title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Ghana: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Ghana: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Ghana: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Organizing legal, healthcare, and financial affairs while managing a serious or terminal illness in Ghana centers on patient rights under the Public Health Act, health coverage rules under the National Health Insurance Scheme, incapacity planning via powers of attorney and wills, social security invalidity applications, and consular legalization for foreign use. Because the Ministry of Health (moh.gov.gh) and Judicial Service (judicial.gov.gh) websites experienced external connection timeouts during verification, this guide cites live portals of the Ghana Health Service, NHIA, SSNIT, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Parliament of Ghana legislative repository, and Hague Conference (HCCH) records.

steps.title: Healthcare Rights, Insurance Benefits, and Medical Records
steps.html:
• Review patient rights to clear medical information, informed consent, confidentiality, and complaint mechanisms under the Patients' Charter (Sixth Schedule, Section 167 of the Public Health Act, 2012, Act 851) through facilities overseen by the Ghana Health Service (GHS) [1].
  • Verify what clinical care is funded through the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) via the NHIS Benefits Package: inpatient care, outpatient consultations, emergencies, and cervical and breast cancer treatment are included, whereas cancers outside those sites and chronic kidney dialysis are among listed exclusions that require separate budgeting or private insurance [2][3].
  • Request formal specialist medical summaries, diagnostic test results, and prognosis documentation early, as employers, insurers, and SSNIT medical boards rely on original clinical evidence [1][4].

steps.title: Powers of Attorney and Will Execution
steps.html:
• Appoint a trusted agent while full legal capacity remains by executing a written Power of Attorney under the Powers of Attorney Act, 1998 (Act 549), signed and dated by the donor (or at the donor's direction in the presence of two witnesses) to authorize specified banking, property, or administrative acts [7].
  • Execute a valid written will in accordance with the Wills Act, 1971 (Act 360), which requires the maker to be at least 18 years old and sign at the foot or end in the simultaneous presence of two or more competent witnesses who also attest the signature [8].
  • Deposit the sealed original will at the High Court Probate Registry for safe custody, and note the deposit details in family administrative files [8].

steps.title: SSNIT Invalidity Benefits and Beneficiary Nominations
steps.html:
• Check eligibility for an Invalidity Pension through the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT): contributors must have made at least 12 monthly contributions within the 36 months prior to the onset of permanent incapacity, obtain certification from a recognized medical practitioner, and attend an assessment by a SSNIT Medical Board [4][6].
  • Update nominee allocations promptly by submitting the official Nominee(s) Details Form via the SSNIT Forms portal so current dependant wishes are properly recorded [5].

steps.title: Asset Inventory and Institutional Records
steps.html:
• Compile an indexed summary of Ghana Card identification, bank and mobile money accounts, property title deeds, Tier 2 and Tier 3 occupational pension statements, and life insurance contracts [5].
  • Keep copies of executed powers of attorney, SSNIT membership numbers, and High Court will deposit receipts accessible to the designated representative [7][8].

steps.title: Document Authentication and Consular Legalization
steps.html:
• Ghana is not a Contracting Party to the HCCH 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so Apostille certificates do not replace diplomatic authentication for documents moving to or from Ghana [11].
  • Route Ghanaian civil status certificates, notarized powers of attorney, or certified medical reports for international use through notarization and Judicial Service certification, followed by attestation at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Accra and subsequent legalization at the destination country's embassy or high commission [9][10].
